newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends off peak, but more strength seen.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends off peak, but more strength seen.

text.p: LME copper floated off its 13-month highs on Thursday afternoon, but the market was expected to regroup and rechallenge the upside, traders and analysts said.
Three months copper ended the afternoon kerb $19 higher at $2,580 per tonne, well off an earlier 13-month peak of $2,609.
"It's still a very good close and some people are talking about seeing $2,800," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.
"My next target is $2,715, the high just before the Sumitomo scandal last year," he added.
Covering against exposed options positions helped prices motor higher in the morning against a background of supply disruptions, traders said.

Some traders said the market had been pushed higher in an effort to squeeze more covering out of a Far East options grantor, but others dismissed the talk, saying the covering could have come from a variety of sources.
Prices got the wind knocked out of them after attaining the morning peak, attributed by some of the sources to an out-of-ring deal between the Far East firm and a big U.S. investment bank.
Spreads narrowed slightly by the end of the day to a $84/$87 backwardation from $100/$105 on Wednesday evening.
Options volume was large, with 18,956 lots of calls traded during the morning session alone, with the bulk of these in calls, LME data showed. Afternoon options volume was not yet available.
The big turnover figures, however, may not represent fresh business, since in the past give-ups among brokers have inflated volume, but left open interest little changed, option sources said.
Open interest data will be available on Friday.
Other metals failed to catch the excitement in copper, most ending softer.
Aluminium shed $8 to $1,615 despite a string of stock drawdowns, including 3,100 tonnes on Thursday.
Selling keeps capping the upside, but the fundamental situation should eventually come to the fore, Adams said.
"Once it absorbs the selling we could see it higher again," he said, adding that his next upside targets were $1,660 and $1,680.
Nickel lost $65 to $7,195, breaching a short-term uptrend and the 10-day moving average.
But with the Inco strike continuing, the downside should be limited, traders said.
Zinc eased by $9 to $1,359, edging to the bottom of its recent range, but managing to remain above the 10-day moving average.
Lead closed barely changed at $635, down $2 while tin finished $10 higher at $5,610.
Alloy ended at $1,483/7, compared to $1,486/90.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
